caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 406 of 2005
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate (J.N. Deb, Advocate With him) instructed by Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners. 
Respondents ------ Not represented.
parties:
Md. Sonawar Ali being dead his heirs; Md. Mobaswir Ali Chowdhury and others ------ Petitioners.
Vs.
Md. Nonahar Ali alias Monawar Ali being dead his heirs; Mozzamil Ali Chowdhury and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 2. The predecessor of the petitioners namely Sonawer Ali, as plaintiff, filed the above suit (previously Title Suit No. 221 of 1978) seeking declaration of his title in the suit land on the averments, inter alia, that the suit land measuring 1.00 acre, originally belonged to Pyari Charan Debnath who died leaving behind son, kunja Debnath, widow, Tarangini Bala; Kunja Debnath sold the suit land to the plaintiff by registered kabala dated 22.10.1956 and Tarangini Bala also executed a deed of relinquishment in his favour on 10th June, 1958 acknowledging the above transfer to the plaintiff by kabala dated 22.10.1956 and since then the plaintiff has been possessing the same exclusively and thereafter the defendant Nos. 1-4 having dispossessed him from the suit land the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 194 of 1958 in the Court of 2nd Munsif, Moulvibazar against them for declaration of title and for recovery of possession which was decreed on contest and the above defendant Nos. 1-4 then preferred Title Appeal No. 208 of 1959 but the lower appellate court, after hearing, also affirmed said decree and the defendant Nos. 1-4 then preferred Second Appeal No. 259 of 1960, before the High Court Division which after hearing was dismissed; in pursuance of the said decree the plaintiff filed Title Execution Case No. 11 of 1965 and in the above execution proceeding the plaintiff got khas possession of the suit land through court; thereafter while in peaceful possession of the suit land the plaintiff, on 27th July 1978, came to know that the suit land has been wrongly recorded jointly in his name as well as in the names of the defendants even though the defendants have no right, title, interest or possession in the suit land and as the wrong recording of the suit land clouded his title in the suit land, hence the suit.
